rationale: C02 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both are presidential letters urging prompt congressional action on pending federal compensation legislation; both justify increases as necessary to recruit and retain capable personnel; and both stress preserving rational pay relationships among grades according to responsibility. The child adapts C02's emphasis on disproportionately inadequate executive and upper-grade salaries into a recommendation for an across-the-board percentage increase that avoids comparatively smaller adjustments for middle and upper grades. C05 shares supporting concepts of recruitment, retention, Classification Act coverage, and coordinated government-wide pay scales, but it lacks the child's closely parallel congressional-advocacy structure. C14 has a similar recruitment-and-retention argument but applies it to teachers and otherwise offers little distinctive shared drafting.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the present emergency demands prompt and adequate adjustment of federal compensation levels as a practical matter so that the government may continue to attract and retain skilled employees of the highest competence
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the efficient administration of the Executive Branch of the Government requires well qualified people for important positions. Because of the inadequate salaries provided for these positions, it has become increasingly difficult for me to get and keep such people.
shared_material.explanation: Both make recruitment and retention of highly qualified government personnel the central practical justification for salary legislation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Federal pay scales in the higher grades tend to be too low in relation to the lower grades for the type of executive responsibilities required.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: it will provide a pattern in which the salaries for different Federal positions have a much more reasonable relationship to the relative responsibilities of those positions than under present law.
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive shared concern with internal salary relationships calibrated to differing levels of responsibility.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I urge most strongly that any increase enacted be on an across-the board percentage basis rather than on a uniform dollar or sliding scale basis, so that disproportionately lower adjustments for the middle and upper grades may be avoided.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: substantial injustices are likely to be done unless the proper relationship between them is maintained. I urge the Senate to act favorably upon this legislation
shared_material.explanation: The child converts the parent's concern about maintaining proper relationships among interconnected pay measures into a specific percentage-based legislative recommendation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The House and Senate Post Office and Civil Service Committees now have under consideration legislation to adjust the compensation of Federal employees. I am writing you to urge that favorable action be taken on this legislation at this session of the Congress.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Senate now has under consideration ... the bills to revise the salary scales of the civilian officers and employees of the Government. ... I urge the Senate to act favorably upon this legislation
shared_material.explanation: The opening situation and operative request closely parallel C02: identify pending federal-pay legislation before Congress and urge favorable action.
